name: examples-integration-v1
purpose: Checks after integrating the 250-example knowledge base. x01 is the observed all-appointments failure (regression, inspected). The 'new' split was written before any run and is not in knowledge_base/examples.sql; several of its patterns resemble examples (noted per scenario), so it measures use of the examples, not unseen SQL shapes. Fixture scenarios with "fixture": "joins" run on evaluation/fixture_db.py JOIN_ROWS. After the intent-preservation step, n02 and x02 are regression cases.

turns: all appointments with Dr. David Taylor for this month, including the patient's name, the invoice amount, and the hospital branch.

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.appointment_id, b.amount FROM appointments AS a LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id LEFT JOIN billing AS b ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id WHERE a.doctor_id = 'D001' AND a.appointment_date >= '2023-11-01' AND a.appointment_date < '2023-12-01'

scenarios.notes: The real data has one treatment and one bill per appointment, so the SQL checks decide; the row comparison cannot.

turns: List only the appointments in November 2023 that have an invoice, with the invoice amount.

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.appointment_id, b.amount FROM appointments AS a JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id JOIN billing AS b ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id WHERE a.appointment_date >= '2023-11-01' AND a.appointment_date < '2023-12-01'

scenarios.notes: Observed: the period was also applied to bill_date (copied from example 249).

turns: Give me every appointment from June 2023 together with the amount of each of its bills; appointments that were never billed must still be listed.

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.appointment_id, b.amount FROM appointments AS a LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id LEFT JOIN billing AS b ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id WHERE a.appointment_date >= '2023-06-01' AND a.appointment_date < '2023-07-01'

turns: Show the June 2023 visits with their bill amounts, including visits nobody was billed for.

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.appointment_id, b.amount FROM appointments AS a LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id LEFT JOIN billing AS b ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id WHERE a.appointment_date >= '2023-06-01' AND a.appointment_date < '2023-07-01'

scenarios.notes: Inspected and fixed after its first run (no longer new). 'Visits' is clarified first because June has Scheduled and Cancelled appointments; the reply chooses every status.

turns: Only invoiced appointments please: one row per invoice with the appointment ID and the amount.

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.appointment_id, b.amount FROM appointments AS a JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id JOIN billing AS b ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id

scenarios.notes: Resembles example 202. The zero-amount invoice B3 must be included.

turns: For each appointment, how many different treatments and how many bills are recorded? Show appointments with none as zero.

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.appointment_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.treatment_id), COUNT(b.bill_id) FROM appointments AS a LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id LEFT JOIN billing AS b ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id GROUP BY a.appointment_id

scenarios.notes: Resembles example 214. COUNT(t.treatment_id) after joining bills counts A4's MRI twice.

turns: What is the total billed per appointment, writing 0 where an appointment has no bills?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.appointment_id, COALESCE(SUM(b.amount), 0) FROM appointments AS a LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id LEFT JOIN billing AS b ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id GROUP BY a.appointment_id
alternative_reference_sqls: SELECT a.appointment_id, COALESCE(SUM(b.amount), 0.00) FROM appointments AS a LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id LEFT JOIN billing AS b ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id GROUP BY a.appointment_id

scenarios.notes: Resembles example 206. Zero is requested explicitly.

turns: What is each doctor's total treatment cost?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.doctor_id, SUM(t.cost) FROM appointments AS a JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id GROUP BY a.doctor_id
alternative_reference_sqls: SELECT d.doctor_id, SUM(t.cost) FROM doctors AS d LEFT JOIN appointments AS a ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id GROUP BY d.doctor_id

SELECT d.doctor_id, COALESCE(SUM(t.cost), 0) FROM doctors AS d LEFT JOIN appointments AS a ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id GROUP BY d.doctor_id

scenarios.notes: D1 has two different treatments with equal cost 100; joining bills duplicates T4a's cost for D2.

turns: Does appointment A2 have an invoice? Show the appointment with its invoice amount.

expect.reference_sql: SELECT a.appointment_id, b.amount FROM appointments AS a LEFT JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id LEFT JOIN billing AS b ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id WHERE a.appointment_id = 'A2'

scenarios.notes: A2 has a treatment and no bill: the answer is one row with a missing (NULL) amount, not 0 rows and not 0.

turns: How much was billed in total for Completed appointments at each branch?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT d.hospital_branch, SUM(b.amount) FROM billing AS b JOIN treatments AS t ON b.treatment_id = t.treatment_id JOIN appointments AS a ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id JOIN doctors AS d ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id WHERE a.status = 'Completed' GROUP BY d.hospital_branch

scenarios.notes: A legitimate billing-first aggregate: must not be flagged by the keep-all check.

turns: Per payment method, how many different patients had bills issued in the second half of 2023?

expect.reference_sql: SELECT payment_method, COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) FROM billing WHERE bill_date >= '2023-07-01' AND bill_date < '2024-01-01' GROUP BY payment_method
